test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

If you will search his pockets you will surely find your watch.
solution:
The correct answer is '**will search**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given above sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The given sentence is an example of the **first conditional sentence**.
 
• First conditional sentences are **used to express situations in which the outcome is likely (but not guaranteed) to happen in the future**.
 
• As per the general rule, in a first conditional sentence, the **tense **in the **"if" clause** is the **simple present**, and the tense in the **main clause** is the **simple future**.
 
• Let’s have a look at the **structural form** of the given rule:
 
 
• **If + subject + simple present + object, subject + simple future + object.**
 
 
 
• **​Example: **
 
 
• ***​**If I **wake up **late, I will miss the bus. (correct)*
 
• *If I **will wake up** late, I will miss the bus. (incorrect)*
 
 
 
• Here,** will research (simple future)** is used in the ** "if" clause **which is wrong according to the rule.
 
• According to the explanation that is given above, ‘**search**’ is the correct use in place of “**will search**”.

**Correct sentence: ***If you **search **his pockets you will surely find your watch.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• * *As per the general rule, in the **third conditional sentence**, the **tense **in the **"if" clause** is the **past perfect**, and the tense in the **main clause** is the **perfect conditional or the perfect continuous conditional**.
 
• Let’s have a look at the** structural form** of the given rule:
 
 
• **If + subject + past perfect + object, subject + **perfect conditional or the perfect continuous conditional **+ object.**
 
• **If + subject + had+ V3 + object, subject + would + have+ V3 + object.**
 
 
 
• **​Example: **
 
 
• ***​**If you **had worked** harder, you **would have passed** your exam. (correct)*
 
• *If you **worked **harder, you **would passed** your exam. (incorrect)*
